title: Towards Retrieving Interaction Spaces for Agentic Search

visual_explainer.question: How can retrieval preserve DCI-style interaction resolution without forcing shell commands to scan the full corpus?
visual_explainer.takeaway: RISE makes retrieval construct a persistent bounded interaction space outside the context window, then preprocesses documents with navigational structure for shell-style local inspection.
visual_explainer.compared_with: Snippet/top-k retrieval and unbounded full-corpus DCI.

analysis.tldr: RISE reframes retrieval as construction of a bounded, re-explorable interaction space: BM25 supplies the corpus boundary, while documents inside the workspace retain verbatim text plus structure for shell-style navigation.
analysis.problem: Top-k snippet retrieval scales but hides evidence operations; raw DCI exposes fine-grained operations but broad shell commands become slow and noisy as the corpus grows.
analysis.core_idea: Retrieve a large persistent candidate set into a per-query workspace outside the model context, then let the agent repeatedly search/read within that set; optionally preprocess documents with line-numbered table-of-contents anchors to improve local navigation.
analysis.agent_loop: generate subquery → retrieve/import candidates → shell-search bounded workspace → targeted read/verify → import more if needed → answer
analysis.retrieval_design: Retrieval is a boundary constructor rather than the final evidence channel. RISE-BM25 isolates the bounded-space effect; full RISE adds navigable document processing.
analysis.evidence: On a 100-query BrowseComp-Plus sample, RISE with gpt-5.4-mini matches raw DCI at 78% accuracy while reducing per-query cost from roughly $1.10 to $0.28. The boundary-only ablation is 1–4 points lower across model tiers, supporting the document-processing contribution at 100K scale. At 1M documents RISE-BM25 remains robust while raw DCI suffers substantial wall-clock failures, although the headline 1M comparison uses different model tiers.
analysis.why_it_matters: RISE resolves the central DCI tension by separating two jobs: global retrieval defines a scalable search region, while local interaction preserves high evidence resolution. It turns 'retrieval vs DCI' into a composable interface design space.
limitations: The full structured RISE system was not run at 1M because TOC preprocessing for the added 900K distractors was not incurred.
The proof of concept uses BM25 and an LLM-based one-time document-structuring pipeline; other boundary and navigation mechanisms remain untested.
Some scaling comparisons across RISE and DCI use different model tiers, so absolute accuracy should not be read as a fully matched causal comparison.
